question: A cell of emf $12\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $1.0\ \Omega$ is connected to an external resistance of $5.0\ \Omega$. The terminal voltage is applied across two parallel plates separated by $2.0\text{ cm}$. A charged particle passes undeflected through the region when a magnetic field of $2.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ T}$ is applied perpendicular to the electric field. Calculate the terminal voltage, electric field between the plates and speed of the particle.

options.A: $V=12\text{ V}$, $E=6.0\times10^2\text{ V m}^{-1}$ and $v=2.4\times10^4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
options.B: $V=10\text{ V}$, $E=5.0\times10^2\text{ V m}^{-1}$ and $v=1.25\times10^4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
options.C: $V=2\text{ V}$, $E=1.0\times10^2\text{ V m}^{-1}$ and $v=4.0\times10^3\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
options.D: $I=\dfrac{12}{5.0+1.0}=2.0\text{ A}$, so terminal voltage $V=\varepsilon-Ir=12-2\times1=10\text{ V}$. $E=\dfrac{V}{d}=\dfrac{10}{2.0\times10^{-2}}=5.0\times10^2\text{ V m}^{-1}$. For undeflected motion, $qE=qvB$, so $v=\dfrac{E}{B}=\dfrac{5.0\times10^2}{2.5\times10^{-2}}=2.0\times10^4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
